title: Railroad Towns and the Quirks of Suburban Development in the GTA
summary: A defining feature of land development in older North American metropolitan areas are the strings of small towns that sprung up along railroad lines radiating out from larger cities. Catalyzed by the construction of a rail station, they grew outwards following a similar model: a main street lined with businesses serving the local community, with a set of compact, walkable blocks of single-family homes surrounding it. Such towns were hubs for surrounding farms and hamlets, and the railroads served as vital economic linkages. Yet as suburban communities began to grow in the post World War II-era, the farms became housing subdivisions full of workers commuting into the city. title: Toronto Generating Station Redevelopment Breaks Ground in Niagara Falls
summary: Construction has begun on the $350-million redevelopment of the former Toronto Power Generating Station just upstream of Niagara's Horseshoe Falls. The privately funded project will restore the National Historic Site and introduce what Niagara Parks describes as Niagara Falls’ first five-star boutique hotel, with free public viewing areas, as well as an art gallery and a museum. Niagara Parks and its development partners marked the start of on-site construction at a Thursday, November 12 ground breaking attended by Ontario’s Minister of Tourism, Culture and Gaming, Zee Hamid.
